title: Simulated concurrent-failure scaling tabletop
content:
Purpose:
This tabletop-style capacity worksheet explores quantitative outcomes for simultaneous region degradation scenarios and asks: how much spare GPU capacity (and of which instance types) must we hold regionally and globally to meet 99.9% token-level availability and keep 95th percentile tail latency within SLO during double-region failure windows?

Scope & context:
- Platform: Redwood Inference hosted + Dedicated hybrid (we operate fleets in us-west1, us-east4, europe-west3)
- Fleet mix baseline: 40% A100-40GB, 45% H100-80GB, 15% L7x (cost-optimized) across regions (capacity fungible via cross-region routing but with higher egress/latency cost)
- Typical steady-state utilization: 62% overall token-weighted GPU occupancy (weekdays peak ~78%)
- Objective SLOs: 99.9% availability for generation calls; p95 latency < 220ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) in-region, acceptable cross-region increased tail up to +90ms on failover.

Assumptions used in simulations (explicit):
1) Failure modes modeled: full-region outage (loss of whole availability zone/region), partial regional degradation (50% capacity loss), and concurrent two-region outage (primary + warm-standby pair).
2) Traffic redistribution policy: smart routing favors region-local; on failover we shift affected traffic to remaining regions weighted by capacity and latency budget.
3) Autoscale latency ramp: cold-start capacity for H100 tasks (heavy quantized models) requires 90s to reach full throughput for new instances; warm-standby has pre-warmed caches (prefix/KV) for 40% of common prompts.
4) Batching behavior preserved: request coalescing unaffected, but effective batch sizes drop during failover, increasing tokens/second per-GPU efficiency drop by 18%-25%.
5) Cost model uses committed vs on-demand mix; reserving spare capacity has a 35% effective discount vs on-demand.

Key variables for runs:
- Reserve ratio r: fraction of fleet held as dedicated spare for DR (0%..30%)
- Cold fraction c: % of spare that is truly cold (not pre-warmed)
- Failover horizon h: window to recover (5m, 30m, 2h)

Simulations summary table (selected scenarios):

Scenario | r | c | fail type | p95 latency delta | availability impact | cost delta vs baseline
--- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---:
Baseline (no extra reserve) | 0% | 85% | single-region outage | +125ms | 99.60% | +0%
Conservative reserve | 18% | 30% | single-region outage | +45ms | 99.92% | +9%
Optimized regional split | 12% | 20% | concurrent two-region (us-west + eu-west) | +110ms | 99.85% | +6.5%
Warm-standby heavy | 8% | 5% | concurrent two-region | +160ms | 99.70% | +4%
Cold heavy, fast recovery | 22% | 70% | concurrent two-region | +95ms | 99.88% | +11%

Interpretation notes:
- Holding ~12-18% effective spare capacity (depending on pre-warm coverage) reduces availability drop under two-region scenarios to < 0.2% from baseline 0.4% but increases committed cost by ~6-11%.
- Pre-warming (reducing c) has an outsized impact on p95 — moving from c=70% -> c=20% cut the p95 delta by ~35% in identical reserve ratios. Prep and cache seeding are high-leverage operational investments.
- Efficiency loss due to reduced batching in failover is the main driver of extra capacity needed: we model a 20% drop in GPU tokens/sec, which scales required reserve upward by factor 1/(1-0.2)=1.25.

Region-level recommended reserve allocation (draft):
- us-west1: 22% reserve of live A100 capacity, prioritized H100 warm-standby pool for latency-sensitive customers (PLG+Tier1). Reason: traffic concentration and low-latency customer base.
- us-east4: 12% reserve, mix of A100+L7x for cost-sensitive burst handling.
- europe-west3: 14% reserve, higher H100 proportion for local privacy-regulated customers.
- Global cold buffer: 6% additional cold capacity on on-demand (not committed) to soak unpredictable tails.
(These %s are of regional live capacity, not global.)

Runbook snippets (actions to take during event):
- Detection (0-30s): auto-detect region health via external probe + route health. Notify SRE channel, kick off incident (INC-DR-<region>).
- Immediate (30s-5m): flip smart-routing to weighted cross-region, enable aggressive prefix reuse, disable background batch jobs to free tokens. Scale up pre-warmed H100 pool (if below reserve target) via hotspot priority.
- Recovery window (5m-2h): if cold start observed, use cross-region fallback to prioritize latency-sensitive routes -> enable partial degrade policy (fallback to smaller model with similar quality for non-critical routes).
- Post-incident (2h+): rehydrate caches, reclock baseline autoscale targets, run causality analysis and token-cost accounting for customer credits.

Operational recommendations (prioritized):
1) Invest in pre-warm automation for top 10 prompt families (expected ROI: reduces required reserve by ~6-8% relative capacity).
2) Implement an on-call fast-path to convert reserved cold capacity to warm within 3m (automation + preloaded KV snapshots).
3) Codify regional reserve targets in provisioning pipelines with tags and quota guardrails so reserved machines are not autoscaled away by cluster autoscaler.
4) Pilot a 12% committed reserve across all regions for 6 weeks and measure real-world p95 during synthetic 2-region failure drills. If observed p95 delta <= 110ms, keep; otherwise increase to 18%.
5) Add per-customer failover tiers in Console: Tier A (latency-critical) pinned to H100 warm pool, Tier B (cost-sensitive) allowed cross-region fallback to L7x.

Unresolved questions / open items:
- How much cross-region egress cost are we willing to absorb for emergency routing? (finance needs input; cost delta modeled but not budget-approved)
- Can we reduce cold-starts further via container snapshotting across instance types? Engineering feasibility unknown.
- What crediting model do Sales/CS want for customer-visible incidents (partial credit vs token forgiveness)?

Quick checklist for next tabletop drill:
- [ ] Schedule 2-hour drill with on-call, SRE, infra, product ops, CS (target: 2025-04-10)
- [ ] Prepare synthetic traffic sets (hot prompts + long-seq workloads)
- [ ] Pre-seed top-10 prefixes into warm pools across regions
- [ ] Configure test routing weights and kill-switch to simulate region loss
- [ ] Capture telemetry and cost snapshots (before/after)

Appendix (numbers & short calc examples):
- Example: baseline global capacity = 1000 GPUs. Weekday peak requires 780 GPUs. With 20% batching drop on failover: effective throughput per GPU drops to 0.8 * normal -> required GPUs = 780 / 0.8 = 975 -> spare need = 975 - (1000 - 780) = 755 - 220 = 535? (note: show full step calc in spreadsheet)
- Placeholder cost snapshot: committed reserve 12% (~120 GPUs) -> incremental monthly cost $265k vs baseline; expected avoidable outage cost (est) $420k for top customers.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working worksheet; numbers are model outputs from the capacity-sim run dated 2025-03-17 and simplified for discussion. Please review assumptions marked above and flag any missing traffic patterns (batch inference spikes, embedded vector workloads).
- If you own a region, chime in on the recommended %s and whether warm/cold split is operationally feasible with current cluster images.

Author: Tara Nguyen (eng-infrastructure)
